title: Session handles are carried in a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie
description: The session handle is transported to the browser as a cookie with Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax set on every issue and every refresh. The cookie is never readable by client-side script. The cookie's Path defaults to '/', its Domain is unset so the browser scopes it to the origin, and its Max-Age reflects the session's absolute expiry. Non-browser clients that authenticate via bearer header are out of scope for this requirement; projects wanting a bearer transport in addition compose a project-level ADR that supersedes the transport half.
rationale: A script-readable session handle is an XSS-to-account-takeover pipeline; a permissive SameSite is a CSRF pipeline. Setting all three flags at the transport layer is the cheapest way to keep the credential out of the DOM and out of the cross-site request path.
